content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: ECC error rate spike detected on gpu-pool-west-1 (threshold 8/min) - multiple XID resets observed

paul_oncall: got the page, I'm looking. metrics show an ECC error cluster spanning gpu-node-17..20, and transient kernel oops on 18. p95 gen latency up ~120ms for Dedicated customers in us-west.

sara_sre: reproing logs now. seeing a burst of Xid 13/31 errors with `nvidia: GPU panic - GPU has fallen off the bus` in syslog. kernel driver v510.XX installed.

ryan_infra: quick check: is this correlated with any recent scheduler changes or kernel upgrades? I don't see recent node pools updates in the last 24h.

mike_runtime: Runtime traces show several container restarts on node-18 due to `OOM` during batch compile. Could be memory corruption triggering ECC alerts and then container panic.

leah_support: Support ticket #INC-4421 reports a customer seeing 502s from Redwood API around 08:12. They have Dedicated capacity pinned to gpu-node-17_18 group. Tracking impact.

paul_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) cordon node-18 and node-19, 2) drain non-critical pods, 3) move Dedicated assignments to fallback pool (gpu-pool-us-east) via routing policy, 4) quiesce batch compile workloads. Who can run cordon/drain?

ryan_infra: on it. running:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-18
kubectl drain gpu-node-18 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl cordon gpu-node-19
kubectl drain gpu-node-19 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
Drains started at 08:18. ETA ~2-4m per node.

paul_oncall: thanks. routing shift: activating policy `fallback-gpu-pool` for affected customers now. mike, can you hold inference rollouts while we stabilize?

mike_runtime: rolling halt set: `redwoodctl rollout pause --env=prod --service=inference`

incident-bot: Notification: Routing policy `fallback-gpu-pool` applied to 3 customer routes (cust-ACME, cust-BEE, cust-CORE).

sara_sre: logs from node-18 after drain: repeated `ECC single-bit corrected (SBC)` followed by `ECC double-bit detected - XID=79` then `nv-hostengine: driver reset` lines. I suspect a progressive ECC fault, maybe a DIMM failing.

ryan_infra: hardware team notified. Opening RMA ticket for node-18 memory. Meanwhile we should quarantines nodes with repeated DBE. I'll taint them: `kubectl label node/gpu-node-18 redwood/quarantine=true`

leah_support: letting customers know: sending quick status: "We detected GPU hardware errors causing transient service degradation; we've moved traffic to a healthy pool and are investigating. ETA for full restoration pending hardware verification." Sending now to on-call account rep. :email:

paul_oncall: customer impact summary for ops channel: ~3% of requests from Dedicated customers returned 502/500s between 08:10-08:20. No data plane compromise suspected; logs and payloads normal. Will follow up if any errors persist after node drain.

mike_runtime: after drain, p95 latency dropped back to baseline within ~90s. However, I see a followup driver reset event on node-20 at 08:25, XID 31. Rolling pattern suggests a background hardware issue rather than a single crash.

sara_sre: agree. two immediate options: 1) evict remaining nodes from the GPU pool and force a cold reboot of the affected hosts (will cause scheduled downtime for associated Dedicated slots), or 2) try soft-recovery via `nvidia-smi --reset` on each NIC/driver instance. Given customer impact, I'd recommend cold reboot for nodes with multiple DBE.

ryan_infra: support for cold reboot. orchestrating with hosts team. pinging ops-oncall and hardware to schedule immediate maintenance window for gpu-node-17/18/19/20. ETA for rebooting each node ~6 minutes, sequential to avoid capacity cliffs.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Maintenance window scheduled: Reboot sequence initiated at 08:32 UTC. Nodes will be taken out-of-service one-by-one.

leah_support: customer notification update: added note that we expect rolling reboots over next 20 minutes, no action needed from customer. Escalating for cust-CORE since they run latency-sensitive workloads.

paul_oncall: handoff note for next on-call (sara): check hardware ticket from RMA, verify node DIMM diagnostics (`memtest`) post-reboot, and confirm dedicated capacity rebind. I'll stay available for major escalations.

sara_sre: copying handoff steps: 1) confirm rebooted nodes come back with clean ECC counters (`nvidia-smi -q | grep -A5 'ECC Errors'`), 2) run memtest overnight on nodes with >1 DBE, 3) if DBE persists, schedule out-of-band replacement, 4) re-run regression evals for affected models.

ryan_infra: reboots in progress. node-17 back online at 08:36, node-18 at 08:44, node-19 at 08:50. node-20 scheduled next.

mike_runtime: monitoring shows no further container crashes after node-18 reboot, but we still have one XID on 20 at 08:53. If node-20 shows more than 1 DBE after reboot, we should RMA.

leah_support: cust-ACME replied: "thanks for quick action, will monitor but seeing improvement". updating ticket.

paul_oncall: wrap-up: routing policy kept customer impact low, cordon/drain reduced noisy restarts, hardware team engaged for RMA on node-18 if memtest fails. Handoff to sara for follow-ups. I'll post postmortem stub in /incidents/postmortems once we have hardware diag. :thumbsup:

sara_sre: acknowledging handoff. I'll own the postmortem and confirm replacement schedule. Adding runbook note: if ECC DBE spike >5 nodes in 10m, trigger cluster-wide evacuation policy instead of per-node drain.

k8s-deploy-bot: Deploy alert: `redwood/inference` rollout remains paused. Resume after oncall confirms stable capacity.

paul_oncall: ending live thread. If anything else flares, reopen with new page.
